title: Jeffries Nominated for House Speaker; Cuellar Backs Him as Democrats Eye Historic First
excerpt: House Democrats nominated Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York for Speaker of the House on Wednesday, Nov. 18, putting him on track to become the first Black speake
content:
House Democrats nominated Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York for Speaker of the House on Wednesday, Nov. 18, putting him on track to become the first Black speaker in American history when the new Congress convenes in January.

Jeffries won the closed-door party vote 251-11, with no other member officially challenging him. Eleven Democrats voted against the nomination; seven of them said afterward they had won commitments from Jeffries on issues including immigration enforcement, Medicare for All and Gaza.

The nomination is not the election. Jeffries must still win a majority of the full House — 218 votes — when the 120th Congress convenes on Jan. 3, 2027. Democrats are projected to hold a comfortable majority after sweeping the midterm elections; The Associated Press has called 257 House races for Democrats and 171 for Republicans, with seven races still uncalled.

Rep. Henry Cuellar, who represents Texas’ 28th District including Laredo, voted to nominate Jeffries and defended the lopsided tally. “We wanted to make sure that people understood that there’s a strong vote,” Cuellar said. “Eleven noes — it is a small group that had to marginalize themselves.”

If elected, Jeffries, 56, of Brooklyn, would be the first Black American to hold the Speaker’s gavel since the House first convened in 1789. He has led House Democrats since 2023 and was the first Black lawmaker to lead either major party in Congress.

The rest of the incoming leadership team would also make history: Rep. Katherine Clark of Massachusetts would be the first woman to serve as majority leader, Rep. Pete Aguilar of California the first Latino majority whip, and Rep. Ted Lieu of California the first Asian American caucus chair.

Democrats say they plan to move quickly in January on bills aimed at ending the war in Iran and rolling back tariffs, Medicaid cuts and immigration policies, according to reporting on the leadership vote.

What happens next is the public floor vote on Jan. 3. With Democrats holding a majority of more than 40 seats, Jeffries enters that vote as the heavy favorite — but the speakership is only his when the full House votes.

Sources: Associated Press, Nov. 18, 2026; The Washington Sun, Nov. 18, 2026; Washington Examiner, Nov. 18, 2026.
